dataset: Decision prerequisites — questions, information, and known answers
note: These are the questions that must be answered before any implementation decision is made. 'What we know' reflects verified information only (with sources). 'What we don't know' reflects genuine gaps; suggested actions are proposals to close each gap, reviewed on the Suggestions page before any change is implemented.

rows.question: Which bet types should be modeled first: single bets, parlays, or player-prop combinations?
rows.why: Bet types have different market efficiency, variance, and data requirements; this determines the entire architecture.
rows.what_we_know: Market-efficiency comparisons place NFL point spreads as the most efficient market and player props/parlays as materially less efficient (wider margins, lower liquidity), meaning props/parlays offer more room for a model edge but are harder to price correctly.
rows.what_we_dont_know: Which bet type matches the intended bankroll, risk tolerance, and available data feeds.
rows.suggested_action: Review Suggestion S01 (phased rollout) and confirm the priority order before implementation.

rows.question: Can we obtain machine-readable official lines, and from where?
rows.why: Every strategy requires real market prices to compute edge; without verified lines nothing can be validated.
rows.what_we_know: Official sportsbook pages are not machine-readable from this environment (BetMGM geo-wall, Caesars/FanDuel HTTP 500, DraftKings 404). The lines table on the Market Data page is intentionally blank and flagged per the no-unverified-values rule.
rows.what_we_dont_know: Whether licensed book APIs, official data feeds, or a monitored scraping pipeline can be legally and technically used in the target jurisdiction.
rows.suggested_action: Review Suggestion S02 (official lines feed) and confirm the data-acquisition path before modeling.

rows.question: What exact pass/fail thresholds define a validation gate for a strategy?
rows.why: Every strategy must pass validation gates before it is allowed on the leaderboard or in live use.
rows.what_we_know: Established edge-qualification practice uses a minimum edge threshold per sport (e.g., NFL 12% per some models, and common grades of A/B based on edge >=2.5% etc.); CLV is the accepted skill metric independent of outcome variance.
rows.what_we_dont_know: The site owner's chosen thresholds, minimum sample size, and holdout rules.
rows.suggested_action: Review Suggestion S03 (gate thresholds) and set the numeric thresholds before any strategy is scored.

rows.question: How do we prove a strategy's results are skill and not luck?
rows.why: The user requirement is to remove luck from the equation; this dictates the statistical methodology.
rows.what_we_know: CLV (closing line value) measures price-finding skill independent of win/loss variance; significance can appear in ~50-100 bets vs ~2,000+ for profit. Luck-adjusted efficiency methods (e.g., Adjusted QB Efficiency adjusting for INT/drop/fumble luck) demonstrate how to strip luck from underlying metrics.
rows.what_we_dont_know: Whether to use CLV as the primary skill metric, plus the acceptable confidence level for declaring skill.
rows.suggested_action: Adopt CLV as the primary skill metric plus a luck-adjusted metric layer; review on the Validation page.

rows.question: Which statistics must be correlated when combining bets (parlays/props)?
rows.why: Correlated legs invalidate naive probability multiplication and can destroy a strategy's true edge.
rows.what_we_know: Legs in a parlay are not independent when they share drivers (e.g., team total and QB passing props, or spread and total); market-efficiency analyses explicitly note correlation modeling matters most in game props and combination bets.
rows.what_we_dont_know: The specific correlation values between our signal families (team strength, injury, situational, market) — not yet computed.
rows.suggested_action: Review Suggestion S04 (correlation matrix) to compute and store correlation values before allowing multi-leg strategies.

rows.question: How do we detect and quantify defense/offense deficiencies from backups (2nd/3rd/4th string) replacing starters?
rows.why: The system must track injuries and the quality drop when backups fill in for starters.
rows.what_we_know: The official NFL.com injury report is verified and machine-readable (Week 10 data collected: 345 rows, all 14 games). Adjusted Games Lost (AGL) is an established method that weights starters over bench and incorporates game-status health to quantify injury impact.
rows.what_we_dont_know: Depth-chart ordering (1st/2nd/3rd string) is not machine-verifiable from NFL.com (depth-chart page 404s); only roster status (ACT/DEV/PUP/TRD) is verifiable. AGL values per team are not yet collected.
rows.suggested_action: Review Suggestion S05 (depth-order data source) to secure a verifiable depth-order feed before deploying deficiency scoring.

rows.question: What are the leaderboard rules, rewards, and fairness constraints?
rows.why: The leaderboard must reward top-performing strategies without rewarding luck or risk-taking.
rows.what_we_know: Fair leaderboards must score on a luck-adjusted, risk-controlled basis (edge/CLV, not raw profit) and use out-of-sample or walk-forward validation.
rows.what_we_dont_know: Reward structure (prize, recognition), season length, minimum bets required, and whether strategies may change mid-season.
rows.suggested_action: Review the Leaderboard page spec and confirm the reward structure before launch.

rows.question: What is the bankroll, unit size, and maximum exposure per strategy?
rows.why: Stake sizing and risk caps determine whether results are comparable and whether drawdowns are survivable.
rows.what_we_know: Quarter-Kelly stake sizing capped at 2% of bankroll is a standard conservative approach used by edge models; Kelly criterion adjusts size to projected edge.
rows.what_we_dont_know: The actual bankroll, unit definition, and per-strategy caps chosen by the owner.
rows.suggested_action: Confirm bankroll parameters; adopt quarter-Kelly capped sizing unless overridden.

rows.question: Which underlying signals feed the line-generation model, and with what weights?
rows.why: Signal selection determines model quality; weights must be learned out-of-sample.
rows.what_we_know: Established signal families: opponent-adjusted EPA ratings (recency-weighted, ridge-regularized), efficiency metrics (DVOA, success rates), strength of schedule, and market-implied information from lines themselves.
rows.what_we_dont_know: The chosen signal set, weights, and whether any weight is allowed to move the market number based on out-of-sample performance.
rows.suggested_action: Review the Strategies page signal table and confirm the initial signal set.

rows.question: In which jurisdiction will betting/modeling operate, and does that change data-sourcing options?
rows.why: Lines availability, data licensing, and promotion of bets depend on jurisdiction.
rows.what_we_know: No jurisdiction has been confirmed. BetMGM's page redirects to a state-by-state geolocator, showing availability is jurisdiction-dependent.
rows.what_we_dont_know: The operating jurisdiction(s), which determines which books are accessible and what data can be licensed.
rows.suggested_action: Confirm jurisdiction before any lines-acquisition or deployment decision.

rows.question: How are unverified values handled and reviewed?
rows.why: The project mandates no unverified values in tables; a review workflow must exist.
rows.what_we_know: Policy: every table row must carry a source link to an official site; values that cannot be confirmed from an official source are left blank and flagged, never inferred. The Flagged for Review page publishes all such items.
rows.what_we_dont_know: Who performs manual review and the SLA for resolving flagged items.
rows.suggested_action: Use the Flagged for Review page as the review queue; assign a reviewer per flagged item.

rows.question: Which site improvements most improve decision-making?
rows.why: The site should be a decision-support dashboard; improvements should be prioritized by decision impact.
rows.what_we_know: The current site provides verified standings, full injury data, decision prerequisites, suggestions, and strategy frameworks. Gaps: verified lines, depth-order, and model outputs are not yet available.
rows.what_we_dont_know: Which improvements the owner prioritizes; see the Suggestions page for the prioritized list.
rows.suggested_action: Review the Suggestions page and pick the implementation order; no change is made before review.

rows.question: What is the strategy lifecycle: backtest, walk-forward, leaderboard, promotion, demotion?
rows.why: Strategies must pass gates before earning rewards and be demoted when they fail.
rows.what_we_know: A staged lifecycle (backtest -> walk-forward validation -> leaderboard eligibility -> promotion) with gate-based demotion is required by the project's validation-gate requirement.
rows.what_we_dont_know: The exact stage thresholds and demotion rules; proposed on the Leaderboard page.
rows.suggested_action: Confirm the lifecycle stages and demotion triggers on the Leaderboard page.

rows.question: How often must standings, injuries, and lines be refreshed?
rows.why: Stale data produces stale signals; refresh cadence is an operational decision.
rows.what_we_know: Injury reports update weekly (Week 10 published for the Nov 12-16 slate); standings update weekly after games; lines move continuously from open to kickoff.
rows.what_we_dont_know: The refresh cadence and automation to be implemented.
rows.suggested_action: Adopt weekly refresh for standings/injuries and continuous for lines once a verified feed exists.
